question: Which independently varied Scoreline payoff, Afterimage payoff, acquisition priority, Faultline rarity and Ward setup levels causally produce two reachable, policy-sensitive Duskblade packages without broad power movement or reliability regression?
decision: Use two mechanism-blocked common-random-number designs and the smallest shared cross-package anchors to select at most one feasible scalar candidate, close the tested scalar family and continue structurally inside issue #421, or stop inconclusive at the frozen cap.
method: five-factor mechanism-blocked common-random-number identification; not the old four-factor design and not a blind joint factorial

entryGate.executionFreeze: Before the first observation, a machine-readable execution manifest must bind this protocol SHA-256, the deterministic runner SHA-256 and the unchanged harness identities above.

scorelinePayoff.low: Remove scorelineBonus from normal and upgraded Faultline while retaining Duskblade Scoreline consumption and remaining-Facet completion.
scorelinePayoff.high: Set normal Faultline scorelineBonus to 12 and upgraded Faultline scorelineBonus to 15, retaining the same consumption and remaining-Facet completion.

afterimagePayoff.low: Set normal and upgraded Warden's Edge reflection to 2 times current Ward when Afterimage is consumed.
afterimagePayoff.high: Set normal and upgraded Warden's Edge reflection to 3 times current Ward when Afterimage is consumed.

acquisitionPriority.definition: Research-only card-reward completion bonus equal to the level times each frozen policy's card.aspectBonus; it is read only when an offered card completes an aspect-valid registered pair already in the deck.

faultlineRarity.definition: Set only cards.executioner.rarity; every other catalogue leaf is identical within the matched content variant.

wardSetupPriority.definition: Research-only combat score bonus equal to the level times each frozen policy's card.aspectBonus, read only for Duskblade Defend while Warden's Edge is held and Afterimage is absent.

physicalAliases: The Q=2 and Q=4 S-low/A-low/R-uncommon/W-2 cells belong to both mechanism blocks and are simulated once.
For each acquisition level, the interference difference-in-differences reuses the shared-low, Scoreline-high-only and Afterimage-high-only cells and adds only the joint-high cell.
conditionalClaims: Scoreline block effects are conditional on Afterimage payoff low and Ward setup 2.
Afterimage block effects are conditional on Scoreline payoff low and Faultline uncommon.
Initial cross-package interference is conditional on Faultline uncommon and Ward setup 2, estimated separately at acquisition 2 and 4.
No unobserved Cartesian-product main effect or interaction is estimable or claimable.
aliasStructure.sharedFactor: Acquisition priority is the same causal factor, policy implementation and two levels in both blocks; it is not duplicated into package-specific knobs.

scorelineBlock: scorelinePayoff x acquisitionPriority: reward completion priority changes how often the payoff-bearing consumer becomes reachable
scorelinePayoff x faultlineRarity: payoff and offer frequency jointly determine realised Scoreline consumption
acquisitionPriority x faultlineRarity: selection priority can compensate for lower offer frequency
afterimageBlock: afterimagePayoff x acquisitionPriority: reward completion priority changes Warden's Edge reachability
afterimagePayoff x wardSetupPriority: consumption payoff and deliberate Afterimage setup jointly determine exploitation
acquisitionPriority x wardSetupPriority: acquisition and combat setup are sequential requirements for the package
crossPackage: scorelinePayoff x afterimagePayoff at each acquisition level: the packages compete for card rewards, hand slots, energy and combat actions
scorelinePayoff x afterimagePayoff x acquisitionPriority: stronger completion priority may amplify reward competition between the packages
mechanisticInteractions.excluded: No other interaction is fitted or interpreted before its exact optional boundary cells are triggered and observed.

cohorts.commonRandomNumbers: Every initial and triggered expansion cell uses every identity above. No cell receives a promising-only cohort, extra seed or different first look.

baseline.rectangles: The same 64 RandomBuild seeds on all four grids and the same 64 policies x 4 seeds on Duskblade Vow 5 are run once and reused for every candidate comparison.
baseline.causalContrasts: Factor effects use matched low/high design cells under identical remaining factor levels; the live baseline is not substituted for a missing factorial corner.

endpoints.scorelineIntensity: For each policy-cell unit, log1p of the mean over four seeds of min(scorelineApplied, scorelineConsumed).
endpoints.afterimageIntensity: For each policy-cell unit, log1p of the mean over four seeds of min(afterimageApplied, afterimageConsumed).
endpoints.routeActive: A policy identity is active for a route when at least one of its four seeds has both the registered applied and consumed metric above zero.
endpoints.routeExclusive: A policy identity is active for one route and inactive for the other in the same cell.
endpoints.policyWin: Mean win indicator over the four seeds for each policy identity.
endpoints.randomBuildWin: Paired win indicator by aspect, vow and RandomBuild seed.
endpoints.fault: Outcome stall or error, or a non-empty error field.
endpoints.duration: Mean combat turns per fight in a whole run; candidate-minus-live is paired on policy identity and simulation seed.

estimator.mainEffects: Average matched high-minus-low difference across every observed context in the relevant mechanism block; acquisition effects are reported once per block and jointly, not treated as two factors.
estimator.interference: At each acquisition level, joint-high minus Scoreline-high-only minus Afterimage-high-only plus shared-low, using the three reused corners and one joint-high anchor.
estimator.uncertainty: Percentile 95% interval from 5000 deterministic cluster-bootstrap resamples; policy identity is the cluster for policy endpoints and simulation seed is the cluster for RandomBuild endpoints.
estimator.standardisation: Mediator effects use the square root of the mean low/high sample variances. If that denominator is zero, an exactly zero raw contrast maps to zero and a non-zero raw contrast maps to signed infinity.
estimator.multiplicity: No p-value fishing or post-hoc model selection. Decisions use preregistered practical thresholds and interval location only.

candidateGate.policySensitivity: Each route has at least 16 active and 16 inactive policy identities among the same 64.
candidateGate.functionalSeparation: Each route has at least four exclusive policy identities in the same cell.
candidateGate.reachability: Each route has at least eight policy identities with a registered consumer consumption event; no diagnostic or injected acquisition path substitutes for the live reward path.
candidateGate.randomBuild: On every aspect-vow grid the candidate RandomBuild win rate is below 0.50, absolute paired movement from the frozen live baseline is at most 0.10, and added faults are zero.
candidateGate.reliability: The policy panel has zero stalls and errors and no candidate-added fault against the matched live baseline.
candidateGate.duration: The upper 95% bound of paired candidate-minus-live mean combat turns per fight is at most 0.25 turns.
candidateGate.vow5: The Duskblade Vow-5 policy-panel win rate is at most 0.90.
candidateGate.admission: Every gate passes on the frozen first-look cohort; no endpoint absent from a comparable rectangle supports admission.

interferenceExpansionRule.mediatorDecisionValue: Trigger when a Scoreline or Afterimage interaction interval excludes zero and its absolute point estimate is at least 0.25 pooled standard deviations.
interferenceExpansionRule.winDecisionValue: Trigger when a policy-win or any RandomBuild-grid interaction interval excludes zero and its absolute point estimate is at least 0.10.
interferenceExpansionRule.reliabilityDecisionValue: Trigger on any joint-high added stall or error.
interferenceExpansionRule.action: If any trigger fires, simulate all 12 optional expansion cells on the complete frozen cohorts. Do not choose a tier, cell or cohort from observed promise. If none fires, expansion rows are exactly zero.

order: cell id ascending as the final exact tie-break
selectionRule.rule: After the expansion decision, intersect all candidate gates and freeze only the first feasible cell in this order for a new independent held-out confirmation protocol. Outcome magnitude never breaks a tie.

successRule: Exactly one or more cells pass every candidate gate after the preregistered expansion decision. Freeze at most the lexicographically first feasible cell for independent held-out confirmation; do not spend holdout or protected seeds under this protocol.
futilityRule: If no cell is feasible, no interference expansion trigger fires or the complete triggered expansion is finished, and every near-feasible cell has at least one gate whose 95% interval cannot cross its practical threshold, close this tested scalar family and continue with the next evidence-backed structural mechanism inside issue #421.
inconclusiveRule: At the 16896-row or 3600-second cap, record inconclusive if any otherwise near-feasible cell still has only interval uncertainty capable of changing its gate, or if an immutable-input mismatch, incomplete CRN rectangle, unavailable engine, cache corruption or harness fault prevents the registered estimands. Do not rerun, add seeds or tune levels under this protocol.

methodBoundary.ml: Not authorised by this protocol. A later method requires this experiment to identify a remaining policy-repertoire bottleneck and a separate measured decision-value justification.
methodBoundary.rl: Not authorised by this protocol. No policy optimiser may replace the fixed identities or change cell cohorts.
methodBoundary.adaptiveTuning: V39-style candidate-by-candidate value tuning, promising-cell extensions and Cartesian completion are forbidden.
